name: CO-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+20 partisan lean anchors a large Democratic edge
Neguse is a well-funded two-plus-term incumbent with $3.1 million on hand
Republican challenger Kelley Dennison shows no reported fundraising or polling support
Prediction markets price Democratic win odds near 98%
model.rationale: This seat's strong Democratic lean, Neguse's incumbency and roughly $3 million war chest against a little-funded challenger, and markets pricing a Democratic win at 98% all point the same way, so the expected margin stays near 25 points for the incumbent.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing the challenger within single digits, or an unexpected external spending surge against Neguse, would be the first sign the race deserves a second look.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Joe Neguse, a Democratic incumbent seeking another term in a district that voted about 20 points more Democratic than the nation in recent cycles, faces Republican Kelley Dennison and Libertarian Gaylon Kent. No public polls or major rating organizations cover the race, but the structural picture is lopsided.

Neguse has raised roughly $2.7 million and holds $3.1 million on hand, while Dennison reports no fundraising totals, leaving her little visible capacity to compete. Prediction markets give Neguse about a 98% chance of winning. With the incumbent renominated without difficulty and no signs of outside spending targeting the seat, the district's strong Democratic tilt should carry him to a comfortable victory in the mid-20-point range.
